data.title: Lisa’s on-screen drinking gets Thais talking about booze law
data.description: Images of Buri Ram-born pop star Lisa drinking Thai beer on a US talk show have sparked discussion among Thais, going beyond her impressive promotion of Thai “soft power” to raise questions about the country’s alcohol advertising law.

data.title: Flash floods hit Phetchabun as Pasak River overflows
data.description: Flash floods inundated communities in Lom Sak district of Phetchabun province after heavy overnight rain caused the Pasak River to overflow its banks, forcing about 300 households to evacuate on Saturday.

data.title: ONE Championship: Kiamran Nabati tells Yod-IQ to ‘polish my belt’ after Nontachai win
data.description: Kiamran Nabati has put himself back in the ONE Championship bantamweight Muay Thai title conversation after rebounding with a unanimous decision over Nontachai Jitmuangnon at The Inner Circle 31.

data.title: Trump signs bill to impose sweeping Russia sanctions
data.description: WASHINGTON - US President Donald Trump signed a bill on Friday authorising new sanctions designed to pressure Russia over its war in Ukraine, after Congress gave its approval after months of delay.

data.title: Western Australia beaches closed after fatal shark attack
data.description: ‌Several beaches along the coast of Western Australia, including in the state capital Perth, will remain closed until at least Sunday, authorities said, after a ​fatal ⁠shark attack at a popular beach in the city on Friday.

data.title: Protesters counter Trump’s Kennedy Center demolition threat
data.description: WASHINGTON - Protesters formed a human chain on Friday around the Kennedy Center, the Washington arts hub that US President Donald Trump threatened to demolish unless his name is restored to it.

data.title: Two defence volunteers killed in Narathiwat attack
data.description: NARATHIWAT - Two territorial defence volunteers were killed and 16 others injured, six of them seriously, when a six-wheel truck carrying them was hit by a roadside bomb and then came under gunfire in Sukhirin district of Narathiwat on Friday afternoon.

data.title: Asian Games to open in Japan after troubled build-up
data.description: NAGOYA, Japan - The 20th Asian Games will open in Japan later Saturday with a glittering ceremony following a stuttering build-up to a multi-sport spectacular that has more participants than the Olympics.

data.title: Death toll from attack at police HQ in Pakistan rises to 31
data.description: KOHAT, Pakistan - The death toll from an explosion and gun attack at a police headquarters in northern Pakistan rose to at least 31, including 16 police personnel, a senior police official told AFP on Saturday, with fighting ongoing.

data.title: Nigerian miners struggled to breathe in cell before 37 died: survivors
data.description: MINNA, Nigeria - Survivors of a Nigerian disaster in which 37 suspected illegal gold miners died while in the custody of a paramilitary civil defence group recounted their panic on Friday as they struggled to breathe inside the cell.

data.title: Drone owners rush to offload gear ahead of Beijing ban
data.description: BEIJING - Drone owners in Beijing flocked to designated buy-back sites this week, looking to sell their devices for as much as possible ahead of an impending citywide ban.

data.title: B20.4bn seizure a highlight of illegal business crackdown
data.description: Thai authorities have seized or frozen about 20.4 billion baht in assets linked to a financial network tied to Cambodian businessman Yim Leak and financier Benjamin Mauerberger, according to an update delivered on Friday.

data.title: White lion cub seized from unlicensed hotel in Chiang Mai
data.description: A Chinese woman was arrested on Friday after authorities discovered a white lion cub at an unlicensed hotel illegally operated and catering to Chinese tourists in Muang district in Chiang Mai.

data.title: Buffett steps down as Berkshire chair on September 18 after over 60 years at the helm
data.description: Howard Buffett takes over as chairman of US group Berkshire Hathaway, while Warren Buffett becomes chairman emeritus and remains a director

data.title: HRH Princess Sirivannavari Presides Over Royal Thai Costume Showcase in Tokyo
data.description: HRH Princess Sirivannavari leads a showcase of Royal Popular Thai Dresses in Tokyo, supporting efforts to secure UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage status

data.title: Over 100 gamblers arrested at two Chiang Mai dens
data.description: CHIANG MAI — More than 100 people were arrested on Friday night when authorities raided two large gambling dens equipped with tight security measures.

data.title: Guru's daily horoscope for Sept 19
data.description: The day of the week you were born on can reveal a lot... Read on.

data.title: ROH Contests GROREIT Asset Sale Resolution, Maintaining Contractual Buyback Rights for Sheraton Hotel
data.description: Royal Orchid Hotel challenges GROREIT’s assertion that its repurchase rights have expired, seeking legal counsel ahead of a critical unitholder vote

data.title: Helicopters battle wildfire threatening Ecuador's capital
data.description: QUITO - Ecuadoran firefighters backed by helicopters on Friday battled a major blaze on a hill overlooking the capital Quito that has led to the evacuation of dozens of people.

data.title: Premier brushes off criticism of EC
data.description: Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul yesterday brushed off criticism of the Election Commission (EC) after it ruled on the Senate collusion case, saying the matter had nothing to do with his responsibilities as prime minister.

data.title: Trust remains elusive
data.description: The main opposition People's Party (PP) may be calling on Pheu Thai to abandon the Bhumjaithai (BJT)-led coalition government, but rebuilding trust between the two parties could prove considerably harder than bringing them together against a common political adversary.

data.title: Nong Khai's new rail run makes debut
data.description: The Transport Ministry yesterday test-ran a rail freight service from Laem Chabang to Nong Khai and back under a public-private model aimed at making Thailand a regional logistics hub.

data.title: B20.39bn seized in nominee network crackdown
data.description: About 20.39 billion baht in assets linked to a financial network tied to Cambodian businessman Yim Leak and Benjamin Mauerberger, also known as Ben Smith, have been seized or frozen, government spokesman Dr Ekkapob Pianpises said.

data.title: Panel backs 4 diseases for watch list
data.description: The National Communicable Diseases Committee has approved a draft Public Health Ministry announcement adding four diseases to the list of communicable diseases requiring surveillance.

data.title: Tighter birth checks target fake fathers
data.description: The Public Health Ministry has tightened procedures for certifying births at public and private hospitals as part of a government crackdown on "fake father" schemes used to obtain Thai nationality unlawfully.

data.title: Household target doubled
data.description: The government has doubled its household solar power target to 10,000 megawatts and will buy surplus electricity at 2.20 baht per unit under 20-year agreements, deputy government spokeswoman Lalida Persvivatana said.

data.title: Crunch time for Spurs and Villa, Dockyard Derby back
data.description: There is a huge match at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium today with a clash between two big Premier League teams that had been strongly tipped for European places but currently find themselves struggling near the foot of the table.

data.title: Kingdom's stars chase redemption on two wheels in Nagoya
data.description: Four years ago in Hangzhou, Thailand's best hope for cycling gold lost it in the final metres -- beaten to the line by a Japanese rider on Chinese soil. Now the rematch comes full circle: the 20th Asian Games are being held in Japan itself, and Thailand's cycling team has arrived determined not to let history repeat.

data.title: Thais target bigger haul than Hangzhou
data.description: Thailand's 694-member team -- a blend of Olympic medallists, world champions, former winners and a host of first-timers -- will head into the Asian Games Aichi-Nagoya 2026 aiming to put on a better show than they did in Hangzhou, China, three years ago.

data.title: Kwanchanok and Miguel are Thailand Amateur Open champs
data.description: Kwanchanok Boonchan and Ilas Miguel won the 92nd Singha Thailand Amateur Open 2026 after yesterday's final round at Panya Indra Golf Club was cancelled because of heavy rain.

data.title: A family affair
data.description: Mah Damba is one of Mali's most revered traditional griot singers, although she is not as well known outside the country as her famous aunt Fanta Damba.

data.title: Chasing the groove
data.description: After post-rock emerged as a major indie sub-genre, exploding in popularity from the early 2000s onwards and inspiring countless bands in Thailand to follow its path, few could have imagined that Tortoise, one of the genre's most revered names, would finally make it to Bangkok.

data.title: Thai Banks Bet on Blockchain to Make Carbon Credits Trusted
data.description: Tokenised mangrove credits and a global registry are moving from concept to pilot – but Veolia warns the hard part is still what happens on the ground

data.title: Spot gold gains 0.3% on September 18 as oil prices fall
data.description: Gold reached a one-week high in global trading and was on course for a first weekly gain in four weeks, despite a stronger US dollar

data.title: Thai spikers, teqball aces seal progress
data.description: The Thai women's volleyball team swept aside Taiwan 3-0 to cruise into the quarter-finals as Pool C winners, capping off a dominant run through the preliminary phase at the Okazaki Chuo Sogo Park Gymnasium in Okazaki City, Aichi Prefecture, on Friday.

data.title: BG Pathum fight back to hold Sailors
data.description: BG Pathum United fought back to secure a 1-1 draw against Singapore's Lion City Sailors in their AFC Champions League Two Group F fixture on Thursday.

data.title: 'Pause' on overt repression in Venezuela, but reforms still needed: HRW
data.description: CARACAS - Venezuela's interim President Delcy Rodriguez has overseen a "pause" in the overt repression of opponents since taking office in January, Human Rights Watch (HRW) said Friday, 18 years after the organization was expelled from the country.
